ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governed by the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10606, as amended), the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 10340), the Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act, and the FSC Regulation on Customer Identification and Verification for Financial Companies. Beneficial ownership information concerning shareholders and managers of a Yuhan Hoesa is reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit through AML/CFT customer due diligence and currency transaction reports; there is no public beneficial ownership register, and disclosure is limited to government authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified extract of the Korean Commercial Register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Commercial Registry / Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A: notarise at a Korean notary public, then obtain Hague Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and present to the accepting authority. Route B: notarise at a Korean notary public, then obtain MOFA legalization and present to the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul, then present to the accepting authority. Routes A and B are parallel alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean tax compliance certificate and current register certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and local District Court Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A: notarisation by Korean notary public plus Hague Apostille by MOFA for Apostille Convention member states. Route B: notarisation by Korean notary public plus MOFA legalization plus consular legalization at the destination state's diplomatic mission in Seoul. The two routes are mutual exclusive alternatives, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation and cross-border IP sub-licensing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial shareholders and board of managers of Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A: notarise the resolution/PoA at a Korean notary public, then apply to MOFA for Hague Apostille and file with the receiving registry. Route B: notarise, then obtain MOFA legalization certificate, then obtain consular legalization from the receiving state's embassy/consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa promoters / notarising Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A: sign before a Korean notary, submit to MOFA for Hague Apostille, then present to the overseas counterpart. Route B: sign before a Korean notary, submit to MOFA for legalization, then submit to the overseas consulate in Korea for consular legalization. Never combine the Hague Apostille route with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a licensed Korean commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank maintaining the provisional corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A: bank branch manager signature, notarisation at a Korean notary public, then Hague Apostille from MOFA for Apostille Convention states. Route B: bank branch manager signature, notarisation, MOFA legalization, then consular legalization at the destination state's embassy/consulate in Seoul. The two routes are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watch-lists, the FATF Public Statements, and the Korea Customs Service denied-persons list before any transaction. The beneficial owner, directors, ultimate shareholder, licensee, and intermediary bank must be checked against PEP databases with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, non-face-to-face entities, high-risk jurisdictions, and politically connected IP licensors. Continuous transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to KoFIU are required within 24 hours of suspicion; a risk-based review is mandatory for all cross-border royalty wires routed through SWIFT.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-Registry (Internet Registry) of the Supreme Court of Korea and the Hometax business name search portal of the National Tax Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean law requires the legal corporate name to be entered in Korean script; an English name may be registered as a trade name but not as the statutory corporate name. The name must follow a four-tier convention: core trade name plus business-objective description plus the legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. Any foreign-language name must be transliterated into Korean phonetically, and the Korean transliteration must be consistent across the commercial register, business registration and bank account; the English name may appear in parentheses. A name must not duplicate any registered company or be misleadingly similar to a government agency or existing commercial entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon provisional rejection, the applicant may file a written objection with the competent district court registration officer within 14 days from receipt of the rejection notice. If the registration officer maintains the rejection, an immediate appeal may be lodged with the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal packet must contain the original rejection notice, a legal memorandum showing no identical or misleading name, and proposed alternative names. Simultaneously, the applicant should file a new name-clearance request with up to three substitute names to avoid delay; the original rejected name cannot be reused unless the fatal cause is cured by an amendment. The entire appeal plus refiling procedure is designed to stay within 7 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an IP HoldCo engaged in patent sub-licensing, Korean banks and the National Tax Service reject a mail-only virtual address. The Commercial Act and the Registration of Place of Business rules require the registered head-office to be an actual place of business with a lease agreement, office signboard and installed communication equipment. Although some registered agents offer virtual business addresses, corporate account opening and VAT registration are routinely declined unless the tenant can produce the original lease and undergo a bank site visit. A serviced office with dedicated lockable room, lease directly in the company's name, and a physically present representative is the minimum acceptable substance; an unregistered postal drop is wholly impermissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk checklist: presence of company nameplate; original lease of at least 12 months; employees or director at the address; business books and IP license contracts; telephone line and e-mail domain; utility bills; signboard matching registration. Quantified probability of unannounced local tax site inspection within 12 months after incorporation: 15% for dedicated leased office; 55% for serviced office; 85% for virtual-only address. The Seoul Metropolitan Government and the National Tax Service share risk data and may deny business place status with retroactive penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as last amended), Articles 545-613 for limited liability companies (yuhan hoesa); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 and 6; Presidential Decree on Foreign Investment; Supreme Court Registration Rules for corporate registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Seoul Central District Court, Corporate Registration Division, for the corporate register; National Tax Service District Tax Office for tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan) together with the prescribed Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Yuhan Hoesa; the initial capital schedule is set forth in the Articles. Funds must be deposited into a temporary subscription account with a licensed Korean bank and may be converted to the corporate operating account after registration. No blocked escrow account is mandated by law; however, if the investor is a foreign national or entity, the inward contribution must be reported in a Foreign Investment Report before or within the grace period prescribed by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_YUHANGHOESA (THE COMPANY), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE SOLE INITIAL MEMBER ON [DATE]. WHEREAS the Company has been organized as a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS the initial member has subscribed to the share capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation; WHEREAS the foreign investment laws of the Republic of Korea permit a non-resident to hold all membership interests subject to reporting; and WHEREAS the Company is formed for the ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents under ISIC 6420 and NAICS 533110. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The capital subscription statement set out in the Articles is hereby ratified. The initial member is deemed to have subscribed in full and shall pay the subscribed capital to the temporary subscription account established at [bank and branch] in the Republic of Korea. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall maintain a corporate won-denominated account and a foreign currency account at [bank]. The bank is instructed to honour cheques, SWIFT wire instructions and royalty receipt and remittance orders executed jointly by the Representative Director and the Corporate Secretary or Finance Officer designated by circular letters of authority. Monthly bank statements shall be reviewed by the statutory auditor, if one is required by law. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is adopted as [address in Seoul, Republic of Korea]. All writs, demands, tax notices and service of process may be served at that address. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease, register the address with the court registry, and file any change with the National Tax Service. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [Name] is appointed Representative Director, [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Statutory Auditor if such office is required under the Articles or the Commercial Act. Each appointee has accepted the appointment and shall exercise the powers and duties prescribed by the Commercial Act and the Company's Articles. 5. CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION AND FEES. The Representative Director is authorized to admit the paid-in capital into the Company's operating account following issuance of the certificate of registered matters, to pay all formation fees, taxes and notarial charges, and to obtain the corporate seal. 6. GOVERNANCE COMMITMENT. No licence, encumbrance, financing or sale of assets having a value above [KRW threshold] shall be concluded without a further board resolution. All decisions with respect to global patent and trademark licensing shall be documented in minutes maintained at the registered office. 7. EFFECTIVE DATE AND CONSTRUCTION. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed in the corporate minute book. In the event of any conflict with the Articles, the Articles shall prevail. ADOPTED this [date] at [place] by unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Notarization, Capital Subscription and Foreign Investment Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Association of Notary Publics / licensed foreign-exchange commercial bank / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) foreign investment desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in a form sufficient to identify the Company's business scope, registered office, capital schedule and officers. Execute the Articles before all incorporators, or their duly authorized representatives, and have the notary notarize the signatures. Then open a temporary subscription deposit account under the Company's intended name with a licensed Korean bank and deposit the agreed paid-in capital. If the initial member is a non-resident, file the Foreign Investment Report with KOTRA or the foreign-exchange bank so that the inward remittance is legally recognized. Obtain a certificate of deposit and the notarized Articles, and preserve these for the court registration step.
required_dossiers: Passport or foreign certificate of incorporation of each member
Power of attorney appointing any local sub-agent
Bank certificate of temporary subscription deposit
Memorandum on beneficial ownership and signatory authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or bank refuses acceptance because identification or translated documents are incomplete, obtain apostilled/certified corporate documents from the member's jurisdiction and the Korean consulate, correct the defective exhibit, and re-submit during ordinary business hours within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court, Corporate Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company to the Corporate Registration Division of the competent district court. Attach the notarized Articles, the bank certificate of capital contribution, a statement of directors/statutory auditor, proof of the registered office lease, the executed power of attorney, and the approved foreign investment report, if applicable. Pay the registration duty and local education tax to the court's revenue officer through the electronic registration system or at the designated bank. The court registrar shall review the dossier for conformity with the Commercial Act and the Rules on Corporate Registration, enter the Company in the commercial register, and deliver a Certificate of Registered Matters.
required_dossiers: List of directors, representative director and auditor
Lease agreement or consent to use registered office
Power of attorney to counsel or local agent
Foreign Investment Report acknowledgment, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of a deficiency order, file a supplemental submission with the court within two weeks and pay any additional fee. If registration is refused, the applicant may petition the court for corrective action or, if necessary, seek administrative appeal within 14 days of written notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, District Tax Office (Business Registration Office) having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court has entered the Company in the commercial register, file the corporate business registration application with the relevant district tax office to obtain a Business Registration Certificate, business tax identification number and VAT vendor status. Present the Certificate of Registered Matters, the corporate seal certificate, the notarized Articles, the lease, and the representative director's identification. The tax office will assign a corporate number for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding and royalty tax matters. For a cross-border IP licensing company, this step also permits the Company to apply for advance tax treaty certification on outbound royalties and to open a dedicated collection account with the National Tax Service for foreign remittance reporting.
required_dossiers: Representative director and auditor identity documents
Application for Business Registration (form prescribed by NTS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the application due to address or officer disputes, submit an amended lease or officer acceptance, obtain the corrected court certificate, and re-file before the statutory one-month deadline. Extensions may be requested by writing to the district tax office chief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal, Bank Account Activation and Office Safety Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court seal registration section / commercial bank corporate division / municipal building fire prevention office (for ordinary office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporate seal with the competent district court seal registration office, because all contracts, licence deeds and bank instruments require a sealed corporate execution. Present the corporate seal registration certificate together with the Certificate of Registered Matters and the NTS Business Registration Certificate to the commercial bank in which the temporary subscription account is held, and convert it into the permanent corporate won and foreign-currency accounts. Obtain the SWIFT banking and e-banking authorizations. Although the Company does not operate a physical factory, chemicals plant, assembly line or warehouse, the Company shall nevertheless confirm that its leased office building holds a valid fire safety certificate, install routine fire extinguishers and emergency exit signs, and notify the municipal fire office of the office occupancy where local by-laws so require.
required_dossiers: Office building owner's fire safety certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or seal office queries the beneficial ownership of the account, file a notarized statement of beneficial owner and supporting passports. If the landlord cannot produce a fire safety certificate, secure a building safety inspection report from the municipal fire department before bank opening. Any AML refusal can be cured by supplying the bank's enhanced due diligence forms within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IP Licence Recordal, Royalty Remittance Clearance and Post-formation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) / Ministry of Economy and Finance (tax treaty and foreign exchange) / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for foreign-investment reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record the Company's ownership and sub-licensing of each trademark and patent with KIPO wherever Korean registration or licence recordal is required, using the prescribed application and payment of publication fees. Prepare intercompany licence agreements, transfer-pricing documentation and royalty certificates. File the foreign investment report, complete the withholding tax certificate application with the National Tax Service, and pass any required cross-border royalty remittance authorizations with the Company's bank so that licence fees may be remitted to and from foreign counterparties through SWIFT. Maintain a board-authorisation register for major licences, and confirm that the Company's minutes, register of members, share ledger and statutory books are held at the registered office as required by the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Patent or trademark certificates and registered ownership
Transfer pricing and royalty valuation memorandum
National Tax Service withholding rate certificate application
Minute book and statutory register ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For any KIPO substantive query, file a written submission or amendment within two weeks; for royalty remittance refusal, submit the KIPO recordal, NTS withholding certificate and updated foreign investment report to the designated bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance for reconsideration. Where the statutory books are incomplete, prepare corrected documents and file an after-the-fact correction with the court if the register has been submitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the Company is a pure intellectual-property holding company performing ownership and cross-border sub-licensing of trademarks and patents under ISIC 6420/NAICS 533110; it does not conduct physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations. If the Company unexpectedly establishes physical premises, the relevant authority would be the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and the local municipal licensing office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial operating, factory, manufacturing or warehousing license is required for the approved business scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — if a physical plant were ever established, the relevant agency would be the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation; for the present pure IP licensing operation no environmental regulator is engaged.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the Company does not own or operate pollution-generating facilities, and a Full Environmental Impact Assessment or Self Environmental Review is not triggered under Korean environmental statutes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the operation generates no process wastewater, cooling-water discharge, VOC fugitive emissions, stationary combustion exhaust, or hazardous waste. Ordinary commercial office HVAC and electronic equipment are not subject to industrial discharge or emissions thresholds; if a future physical operation is created, the mandatory quantitative thresholds under the Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act and Wastes Control Act would then apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no civil-defense fire permit, structural load inspection or workplace-safety approval is required for a patent/trademark licensing holding company without a factory, warehouse or assembly line. If the Company leases commercial office space, it must obtain from the building owner a valid fire-safety certificate, install fire extinguishers and evacuation signage, and apply general duties under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office personnel (electrical safety, sanitation and emergency procedures). The Seoul Fire Department standard special fire safety management certification is not required unless the future business changes to physical operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic tax portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity or a newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the business operator must register for tax purposes by filing an application for business registration with the competent district tax office or through the NTS HomeTax online portal. The application requires submission of the articles of incorporation or foreign company registration certificate, proof of the domestic place of business or domestic tax representative appointment, power of attorney, identification of the legal representative, and, where applicable, foreign investment reporting documentation. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number which functions as the Corporate Income Tax ID and VAT ID. Registration must be completed within 20 days of business commencement; upon approval, the registration certificate is issued and the same number is used for VAT returns, electronic tax invoice issuance, corporate tax filings, and customs clearance documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a check-the-box entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is taxed as a standalone domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. Limited optional consolidated corporate filing is available for wholly-owned Korean subsidiaries only under strict statutory conditions, and hybrid mismatch rules apply under domestic tax law to neutralise deduction with no inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold applies. Any person engaged in a business supplying goods or services in South Korea is mandatorily required to register for VAT regardless of turnover level. Small businesses with annual taxable turnover below the statutory simplified taxable person threshold (generally KRW 80 million) may be subject to simplified VAT assessment procedures, but VAT registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea mandates the issuance of electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-invoice system. Electronic invoices are transmitted to the NTS in near real time using API/EDI integrations; the NTS validates and assigns an approved electronic invoice number with a digital security seal. There is no pre-clearance fiscal authorisation model, but anti-fraud controls are implemented through mandatory e-invoice issuance deadlines, invoice matching, digital time-stamping, and mandatory cash receipts for qualifying B2C transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying services are statutorily zero-rated under the Value Added Tax Act. For IP and patent licensing, zero-rating applies when the IP is supplied to a non-resident licensee for use outside South Korea, and the supply is not made to a permanent establishment in Korea. Claiming the 0% rate requires demonstrable foreign use of the licensed rights, receipt of consideration in foreign currency from the non-resident licensee, and contemporaneous documentation evidencing the cross-border nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit zero-rated export claims and, if the supply is not fully substantiated or foreign currency repatriation is not evidenced within the statutory period, will reassess VAT at 10% on the supply value with retroactive effect, together with additional tax penalties, interest, and surcharges. Fraudulent or false zero-rating claims may trigger criminal penalties through tax evasion prosecution, including fines or imprisonment, and the taxpayer bears the burden of proving export delivery, foreign currency settlement, and foreign use of the IP rights.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the licensing and oversight authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree; operational FX supervision is delegated to the Financial Services Commission and the Financial Supervisory Service, with all reporting executed through designated foreign exchange banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains current account convertibility for normal trade and service transactions, including patent royalties, trademark licensing, and other IP-related commercial flows, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. By contrast, capital account transactions such as foreign direct investment, overseas deposits, loans, securities acquisition, and profit repatriation are subject to mandatory declaration or prior approval through a designated foreign exchange bank. The Korean won is not freely convertible outside the jurisdiction; settlement must be routed through licensed local banking channels, and every remittance must be supported by real underlying trade or service evidence. Foreign investors are not generally prohibited from repatriating profit, but dividend remittances require certified earnings allocation by the board of directors, proof of distributable statutory earnings, tax withholding clearance, and an approved foreign exchange report. Repatriation of invested capital upon equity disposal or liquidation also requires retrospective filing through the custodian bank. During periods of severe market volatility, Korean authorities may impose emergency controls on foreign exchange positions, payment periods, and surrender requirements. Practically, the onboarding and transaction-reporting burden is substantial, and all IP royalty flows must be documented with purpose codes and supported by contracts to avoid administrative fines and foreign exchange transaction penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters, including IP licensors earning foreign currency royalties, must collect all proceeds from foreign counterparts through a designated foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of the export declaration or the provision of services, unless an extension is granted by the authorities. There is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring foreign currency to be exchanged into KRW; however, 100% of the invoiced foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated into Korea and either deposited into a foreign currency account or converted to KRW through the settlement bank. The actual receipt and settlement must be reported in a timely manner under the Bank of Korea's balance-of-payments reporting framework; failure to adhere to the one-year collection timeline or to repatriate the full invoice amount may result in administrative sanctions and customs penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI and multi-currency wallet providers are effectively barred from acting as the principal foreign exchange clearing counterparty or account-holding institution for a Korean-resident entity because they do not hold a foreign exchange business entity license from the Korean authorities and cannot execute Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reports. A fintech EMI can only function as a technical interface or front-end aggregator wrapped around a fully licensed onshore bank, and even then the legal account relationship and SWIFT-clearing responsibility must remain with a local commercial bank. For this global IP patent licensing vehicle, the prudent and compliance-safe approach is to open a multi-currency operational account directly with a tier-1 Korean bank and treat EMIs as supplementary payment dashboards rather than core treasury rails. Therefore, the viability rating for standalone offshore EMI onboarding is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Supervisory Service allows non-face-to-face account opening using accredited Korean digital identity certificates and video interviews, but in practice tier-1 Korean banks require at least one statutory director or an authorized financial attorney-in-fact to appear physically at the branch for the initial account activation. Pure remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted and is generally unavailable for the first operating account. If a foreign director cannot travel to Korea, the bank will typically accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, plus a video interview with the compliance officer, a certified corporate registry excerpt, director identification documents, and company seal certificates. The statutory directors of the Korean LLC must demonstrate direct management authority; a bare shelf director with no economic substance will trigger enhanced due diligence and likely rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk IP holding structure with no visible local economic footprint: the entity is registered under ISIC 6420 as a passive patent/trademark licensor, which may be treated as a shell or conduit for cross-border royalty diversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a certified Korean corporate registry excerpt; audited or internally prepared operating statements showing administrative activity; board resolutions appointing management; ownership and control chain diagrams; patent and trademark registration certificates from KIPO and major international registries; notarized IP assignment and license agreements; source-of-wealth evidence for the capital introduction; and a business plan explaining the group's global licensing structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to definitively identify and verify the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), especially where foreign corporate shareholders form an opaque chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide apostilled corporate registry extracts for each shareholder; certified passports or national identity cards of every qualifying UBO; a documented UBO declaration stating all natural persons holding a 10 percent or greater beneficial interest; foreign economic substance documentation such as tax residency certificates, office leases, and employee lists; and a notarized organizational chart certified by each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty inflows into Korea do not correlate with underlying customs declarations, logistics data, or any visible service performance, creating a negative-risk profile for trade settlement reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the full executed license portfolio: global licensing and sub-licensing agreements, per-territory royalty calculation statements, usage and sales reports from the licensees, annual royalty certifications by independent accountants, IP registration renewal certificates, correspondence confirming the commercial rationale, and a certified IT system report showing license fee invoicing and collections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transfer pricing mismatch between the Korean IP owner and affiliated overseas licensees could cause the bank to suspect tax evasion and mispriced foreign currency remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble the OECD-compliant Master File and Local File for AFC purposes, intercompany service level agreements, the latest Korean tax filing of the entity, VAT zero-rated export tax invoices where applicable, the bank's SWIFT MT103 receipts, the external auditor's comfort letter, target license royalty benchmarking studies, and an independent patent valuation report supporting the arm's length royalty rate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from the foreign parent company must be routed by SWIFT MT103 to a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea with the correct balance-of-payments purpose code for cross-border direct equity investment. The bank will register the transaction under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and issue a foreign currency deposit certificate evidencing receipt of the cross-border proceeds. Following the share allotment, a licensed Korean accountant must perform capital verification against the bank's SWIFT advice, the foreign currency deposit certificate, the board resolution, and the updated corporate registry. The Korean company must also file the required foreign investment report through the designated bank to avoid classification as unauthorized borrowing or irregular remittance. All funds should be held in a defined Capital Escrow Account until the statutory foreign investment registration or shareholder notification has been completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and royalty-related disbursements from Korea, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers covering licensing fees and intercompany disbursements. For physical goods embedded in the licensing model, a commercial letter of credit issued by a Korean bank or confirmed by an overseas correspondent bank is acceptable, together with transport and customs documents. Documentary collections are permissible for lower-risk trade flows but carry greater non-payment and documentary compliance risk. All outbound disbursements must be reported to the designated bank under the Bank of Korea's foreign exchange reporting framework, with the correct BOP purpose code for royalty payments or goods trade, and supported by the relevant license agreement, tax invoice, customs declaration, or board-approved intercompany settlement statement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore FX forward contracts executed with a domestic tier-1 bank against real underlying IP royalty exposure, up to traditionally 100 percent of the documented underlying exposure, with settlement on the maturity date in KRW or the convertible foreign currency.

Currency options and cross-currency interest rate swaps used solely for hedging balance sheet foreign exchange exposures arising from the patent licensing operation and cross-border intercompany loans, subject to the bank's internal derivative eligibility assessment.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not an available hedging substitute for the Korean-resident entity in the domestic market; NDFs are generally reserved for non-resident counterparties in the offshore market, and domestic hedging must be executed through licensed onshore derivative products or permitted over-the-counter instruments booked by the designated bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Amount Return (annual corporate tax return), including cross-border patent royalty and transfer pricing schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, through the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year, no later than 31 March. If the return is prepared and signed by a licensed tax agent, the deadline extends by up to one month (to 30 April).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an unfaithful-return additional tax of 20% of the assessed corporate income tax for willful non-filing and 10% additional tax for ordinary underreporting, plus a late-payment surcharge accruing at 0.022% per day on unpaid tax. Intentional concealment or false invoices may trigger an additional 40% penalty. If a Korean entity remains tax-delinquent, unreachable, or fails to file for a substantial period, the NTS may cancel the business registration certificate and the competent Registration Court may initiate administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporation Income Tax Surtax Return (local income tax on corporate income) integrated with the national corporate return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the competent provincial or city tax office, with remittance administered by the National Tax Service through HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory filing deadline as the corporate income tax return; 31 March for a calendar-year entity, or 30 April when using an authorised tax agent extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The local surtax is self-assessed in the national return; late payment attracts the same 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge and additional local tax penalties not exceeding 75% of the local surtax, plus seizure and compulsory collection; persistent delinquency can cause registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Annual Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, with a copy to the shareholders or members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (30 June for a 31 December fiscal year); the audited financial statements must be approved at the annual meeting no later than 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or submit the audit report to FSS exposes the company to an administrative fine up to KRW 50 million (approximately USD 38,000) imposed by the FSS; the audit report may be deemed a legal nullity for financial statement purposes, and shareholders or members may petition the court for a special audit and, in an extreme case, judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Members' Meeting, Financial Statements Approval, and Statutory Minute Book Documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing; records must be kept at the registered office and produced on demand to any member, registrar, or tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual members' meeting must be held by 31 March for a calendar-year LLC, being within 3 months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the meeting is not convened, any member may obtain a court order requiring it; directors or managers are subject to administrative fines under Commercial Act Article 635 of up to KRW 5 million, and a persistent deadlock can be grounds for judicial strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Management Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), delegated by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (by 31 March for calendar-year entities); any foreign share transfer or foreign-investment modification must be reported within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing is punishable by an administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million (approximately USD 1,500); repeat non-reporting can result in removal of foreign-investment protection and tax treaty benefit claw-back, and if the entity is inactive, administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Secretarial Register Audit and Compliance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The company's registered office and external corporate secretarial partner; not filed with a government agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: To be completed no later than 31 March each year, before the annual members' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty is imposed; however, deficits in required statutory registers are punishable under the Commercial Act by administrative fines of up to KRW 2 million per register and can weaken the evidentiary presumption of recorded resolutions, increasing exposure to court-appointed audits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified CPA audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies where total assets at the close of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 5 billion (approximately USD 3.8 million at 1,300 KRW/USD); for fiscal years 2020, 2021 and 2022 the phase-in thresholds were respectively KRW 10 billion, KRW 8 billion and KRW 6 billion. There are no autonomous turnover or headcount triggers for a private Korean LLC; however, the Financial Supervisory Service may additionally designate any company for a statutory audit upon finding a serious risk to investors or undue related-party arrangements, and an IP-holding company with global patent royalty flows will commonly be audited in practice to substantiate cost attribution and Korean transfer-pricing position.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Companies required to be audited must prepare financial statements under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), which are IFRS as adopted by Korea. Non-audited small or medium entities may elect Korean SME Accounting Standards or the General Business Accounting Standards (previously K-GAAP), but must reconcile to K-IFRS if any audit threshold is met or if the entity is designated for audit by the FSS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Korean legislation, a private Yuhan Hoesa does not file a standalone annual UBO return to a central registry except as follows: (a) a foreign-invested enterprise must include in its annual management status report to KOTRA accurate details of ultimate foreign shareholders, filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; (b) any transfer of shares, including a non-resident IP HoldCo transfer, must be recorded in the Register of Members immediately, reported to the NTS under foreign-transaction reporting where it involves a non-resident, reported to the Registration Court for capital or ownership changes within 2 weeks, and re-filed with KOTRA within 30 days; (c) tax authorities may require substantial-owner declarations and actual-transaction documentation in connection with royalty and dividend withholding at the time payment is made. The annual confirmation protocol is therefore a combined 31 March foreign-investment management report and internal statutory register sign-off; this fulfills the practical equivalent of annual UBO confirmation for the IP licensing structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Member Register of a Yuhan Hoesa)
Register of Directors and Statutory Auditor, if appointed
Register of Charges or Mortgages over the Company's Property
Corporate Minute Book containing minutes of annual members' meetings and management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for a Seoul registered agent or registered office; USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 per year if substantive office presence with a local general manager is required for IP holding substance.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - USD 20,000 for a certified CPA audit of a cross-border IP licensing Yuhan Hoesa under K-IFRS; no audit fee is statutorily payable if the company remains below the KRW 5 billion asset threshold and no FSS designation occurs.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national corporate income tax (progressive: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax (resulting in a maximum combined effective headline rate of 23.1%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Technology transfer/royalty income from patents, know-how, or protected industrial IP may qualify for a 50% income tax reduction under Article 12-2 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; designated R&D expenditure benefits from tax credits (up to 30% for newly growing technologies and 5% to 10% for ordinary R&D); Free Economic Zone and Global Enterprise Zone investments are eligible for a 5-year corporate tax reduction and a further 50% reduction for the next 2 years; intellectual property leasing income may qualify for special deferral or exemption rules for small and medium enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세 과세표준 및 세액계산서) together with the Local Income Tax Return (지방소득세 신고서), filed electronically through the HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) national tax electronic filing portal, with the local income tax return separately filed through the local government's WeTax system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly preliminary corporate tax payments for taxpayers whose prior-year taxable income exceeded KRW 50 million)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year corporate taxpayer, the annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 of the following year; for a company with a different fiscal year, filing is due within 3 months from the end of its fiscal year, and preliminary quarterly returns are due by the end of the month following each quarter

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identity, including corporate name, business registration number, tax identification number, headquarters address, representative director, industry code (e.g., ISIC 6420, NAICS 533110), and fiscal year-end designation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Korean entity's exact Legal name as registered in the Korean Commercial Register; identify non-resident shareholders and all ultimate beneficial owners with CRS/FATCA declarations; any mismatch between the registration and the beneficial owner may trigger immediate MLRI screening under the 'unclear-shell' risk profile of the IP holding company structure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income per financial statements as prepared under Korean IFRS or generally accepted accounting principles, including revenue from patent licensing, trademark royalties, and sub-licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border royalty revenue from Korean and foreign sources must be aggregated; related-party license transactions must be reconciled with the transfer-pricing adjustment schedules; omission of non-Korean source passive income that is attributable to a Korean IP HoldCo will be treated as intentional mis-declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments: non-deductible expenses, tax-free reserves, and statutory addbacks, such as entertainment expenses in excess of limits, donations, certain interest, and fines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an IP holding company, disallowed items commonly include management fees paid to a non-resident related party without supporting services, royalties paid to low-tax jurisdictions without substantive business substance, and expenses corresponding to income not subject to Korean tax; adjust under Corporate Tax Act Articles 19 to 34 and preserve arm's-length evidence for every disallowed item.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilization, foreign tax credit, CFC inclusions, and other non-refundable credits; net operating losses may be carried forward for 5 years for this entity classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits only where a bilateral tax treaty provides for credit without a refund process; CFC rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 6 will impute the undistributed income of a 0% or low-taxed foreign subsidiary to the Korean IP HoldCo where no economic substance exists; attach the loss carryforward schedule and CFC calculation worksheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of national corporate income tax base by applying the progressive statutory rates: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% for KRW 200 million-20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the provisional tax after applying the technology transfer tax reduction (Article 12-2 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act) and any exemption for export-derived IP income; for outbound licensing, ascribe the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) to the Korean entity to maintain the preferential rate; review whether a Patent Box equivalent registration is required before claiming the reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge calculated at 10% of the national corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the 2.1% effective local surcharge separately on the local income tax return; failure to synchronize the local return with the national return on same amounts triggers cross-assessment discrepancies; for non-resident direct licensors, ensure local surcharge is withheld together with national withholding tax on outbound royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax summary for dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident related parties, together with tax treaty relief applications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each outbound payment, attach the non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the treaty article invoked (e.g., Korea-US treaty Articles 10, 11, 12). If the statutory WHT was withheld without treaty relief, file a refund application within 3 years before the expiry of the statutory claims period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: schedule of intercompany transactions, amounts, pricing methods, comparables, and confirmation of Local File / Master File / Country-by-Country Report obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If royalty and other intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceed KRW 10 billion, the Local File and Master File must be filed within 45 days of the annual tax return due date; failure to submit leads to denial of the deduction plus a penalty of up to 30% of the adjusted amount, and the tax authorities may apply the `most appropriate method` assuming a 0% arm's-length return if documentation is missing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers a penalty of 20% of the underpaid corporate tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent or false returns under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2; unpaid tax is additionally subject to a daily overdue surcharge of 0.025% (approximately 9.125% per annum); failure to pay the local income tax surcharge adds a 10% surcharge on the local tax penalty; late filing of TP Local/Master File or failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation triggers a penalty of up to 30% of the adjustment amount, and intentional under-reporting of non-resident withholding tax carries a criminal evasion liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on gross dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident corporation, unless reduced under an applicable bilateral double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must file a Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction Application (Form 20 or 21 as applicable) with the payer or the National Tax Service before the remittance date; the application must be accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence country's competent authority, a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is not a conduit or back-to-back intermediary, and documentation of the royalty, interest, or dividend source. The Korean payer must verify the recipient's economic substance; the tax authority has the right to deny the treaty benefit if the non-resident has no substantive business or is a shell entity under the substance-over-form doctrine. If relief is denied, the taxpayer may file a refund claim through the Korea Tax Tribunal or a bilateral competent authority procedure under the DTA, within the statutory 3-year time frame.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are statutorily subject to 22% WHT (20% + 2% local surcharge), but treaty-reduced rates are typically 10% (e.g., under the Korea-US and Korea-Germany DTA); interest paid to non-residents is statutorily 22%, reduced by treaty to 10% (including Korea-US; 15% in some new DTAs when paid to a non-bank recipient), and a 0% rate is available for certain government or central bank securities; all treaty-rate claims require prior TRC and beneficial ownership filing.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion per fiscal year for intercompany transactions with foreign related parties triggers mandatory Local File and Master File submissions; a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more; documentation must be filed within 45 days after the annual tax return due date.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, judicial anti-avoidance rules, CFC legislation under the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 6, and treaty anti-abuse provisions mandate that an IP HoldCo must show actual personnel, office premises, decision-making, risk control, and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) within Korea to benefit from DTA relief and arm's-length transfer pricing; a mere paper entity or passive dormant recipient of royalties from foreign licensees will be ignored for Korean tax purposes, with income imputed to the actual shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of cross-border patent sub-licensing revenue from the Korean corporate income tax return, including under-reporting royalty income, fabricating intercompany expenses, and using falsified invoices from a zero-tax jurisdiction to reduce the Korean taxable base, while continuing to remit dividends to non-residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, a person who fails to report taxable income in excess of KRW 300 million may be imprisoned for a term of 2 to 5 years and fined up to 3 times the evaded amount; additionally, the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2 imposes a 40% negligence penalty on under-reported taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized or failed to prevent the evasion are subject to piercing of the corporate veil under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 39, making them jointly and severally liable for the full unpaid corporate tax and fines; criminal conviction leads to imprisonment, forfeiture of personal assets, and a travel ban (blacklisting) by the National Tax Service and the Ministry of Justice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure / Statutory TP Penalty
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IP HoldCo engages in cross-border royalty transactions with a non-resident parent or sister company exceeding KRW 10 billion in aggregates, but fails to prepare, retain, or file the Local File and Master File, or arms tests the amount charged using no legitimate comparables and entirely disregards the arm's-length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 11 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, failure to submit transfer pricing documentation triggers a penalty of up to 30% of the adjusted amount, and unauthorized royalty deductions may be denied in full; the payer may additionally face a 20% penalty for under-declaration of taxable income under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the amount of tax underpaid in proportion to their control, with civil asset restitution reaching the entire Benami-omitted sums; a wilful TP violation constitutes tax evasion for criminal purposes, leading to personal fines and imprisonment of up to 5 years, in addition to professional disqualification as a continuing director under the Commercial Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Beneficial Ownership Abuse / Treaty Abuse and AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean IP HoldCo has no employees, no physical office, no bank account with independent control, and no substantive CIGA, yet claims reduced withholding tax under a DTA on outbound dividend, interest, and royalty remittances to foreign shareholders, while bill-and-route transactions funnel Korean-sourced royalties through a zero-tax jurisdiction without any risk or decision-making function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea's substance-over-form doctrine under Article 4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes allows the tax authority to disregard the entity and deny treaty benefits; Article 6 of the International Tax Adjustment Act imposes CFC taxation on the undistributed passive income of the shell entity; and under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act, failure to disclose true beneficial ownership exposes the company to a statutory fine and amendment of the AML registration, while a false TRC claim may trigger fraud penalties and extension of the statute of limations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participated in the shell arrangement are personally liable for restitution of all unpaid withholding tax and local surcharge amounts plus interest; the courts can pierce the veil to execute against personal assets; directors also face travel blacklisting, a civil extended liability under Commercial Act Article 399 for damages to other shareholders, and criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for organised evasion or abuse of the cross-border payment system.
